top_concerns: Binary, small, synthetic benchmark with an always-American option; the steering vector may just learn 'pick non-American'
EI-Gap confounds language and context effects; a single cultural word closes the gap, which suggests prompt sensitivity rather than knowledge
Diversity and stereotype claims rest on tiny embedding-similarity differences and unvalidated LLM-judge rankings; steering may simply localize less
Mechanistic and steering analysis is on one model (Gemma-2-9b-it) with no random-vector or non-cultural controls, and unclear hyperparameter selection
Universal-vector and 'conserved across languages' claims are overstated: modest gains, only 5 languages, and the authors admit no rigorous evaluation
